title: Turtle Compass
summary: Wind, bend and switch coils of wire so a sea-turtle hatchling feels the magnetic field of home and swims for the open sea.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 4.4, Magnetic field due to a current element, Biot-Savart law
concepts: Biot–Savart law for a current element
Field at the centre of a coil, B = μ₀NI/2R
Right-hand thumb rule for the field of a loop
Field of an arc; leads in line with the centre add nothing
Field on the axis of a coil falls off
learningOutcome: The student can find the size and direction of the field of a current element, a coil, an arc and two coils with one centre, and how the field on a coil’s axis falls off.

levels.title: The trim wire
levels.adds: Baseline: dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl sin θ/r², pointing along dl × r (Example 4.4).
hints: μ₀/4π = 10⁻⁷ T m/A. Change dl and r to metres, and give the field in nT.
Only the part of dl across the line to the probe counts: sin θ.
Point your fingers along the current and bend them towards the probe: the thumb shows whether the field points up or down.

levels.title: Wind the coil
levels.adds: New idea: every turn of a tight coil adds μ₀I/2R at the centre, so B = μ₀NI/2R (Ex 4.1, Example 4.6).
hints: B = μ₀NI/2R with R in metres, so N = 2RB/μ₀I.
μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m/A, and 1 µT = 10⁻⁶ T.
Curl your right fingers along the current: the thumb gives the field. Anticlockwise seen from above points up.

levels.title: Bend an arc
levels.adds: New idea: an arc gives its fraction of the loop field, and straight leads in line with the centre give none (Example 4.5).
hints: For a lead that points at the centre, dl × r = 0.
An arc of φ degrees gives φ/360 of μ₀I/2R.
Send the current round the other way and the field reverses.

levels.title: Raise the tank
levels.adds: New idea: on the axis B = μ₀NIR²/2(R² + x²)^(3/2), which falls off from the centre value μ₀NI/2R (Section 4.5).
hints: At x = 0 the axis formula gives the centre value μ₀NI/2R.
The higher the tank, the weaker each turn’s field, so the more turns you need.

levels.title: Two coils
levels.adds: More steps: coils with a common centre add their fields when the currents go the same way and subtract when they are opposite.
hints: Same sense: the fields add. Opposite senses: they subtract, and the bigger one decides the direction.
Work out what the outer coil must add or take away, with its direction.
Then N = 2RB/μ₀I for the outer coil alone.

misconceptions: The field of a coil at its centre does not depend on the number of turns
A straight lead pointing at the centre adds the most field
The field on the axis of a coil is the same everywhere along the axis
Currents in opposite senses in two coils add their fields
A current element makes a field along its own length
